title: So Concludeth the Epistle
subtitle: Chase, chase, chase away, until the road's end is also left behind.

items.text: So Concludeth the Epistle

items.speaker: "Roland"
items.text: "Hahaha, evil giant, tremble in fear, for today you shall meet Sir Roland in the field."

items.speaker: "Roland"
items.text: "Now your devil's luck has run thin!"

items.speaker: "Roland"
items.text: Mr. Knight, are you entirely sure this is Sir Roland's line?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Ahem …

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone reminds you that Sir Roland then was still a spirited young man.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: It was time now to face the giant.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: The giant was just as the letter warned and more, for Felgert was of a monstrous height, and his bare skin was covered with mange and pustules.

items.speaker: "Roland"
items.text: "Allow me!"

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Sir Roland spurred his horse onwards and charged Felgert.

items.speaker: "Roland"
items.text: Uh, Mr. Knight, how can I spur my house? Do you see any horses about?

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Hm ... a fair point indeed.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Perhaps Someone will seek the aid of Mr. Darley Clatter to play the role of Roland's steed.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Yet in the meantime, you need to only pretend to be riding a horse.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: As you say your next line.

items.speaker: "Roland"
items.text: "Bedeviled giant, today you face your doom!"

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Sir Roland cried out at the pinnacle of his charge.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: As he raised the Everlasting Sword high and brought it down on the giant's ankle—

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: The blade collided with the giant's ankle, sliding as if across a sheet of uneven metal, sending forth a shower of yellow sparks.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: The blow had left the giant entirely unharmed. It served only to set the brute into a fitful anger.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: The giant reached out his hand, snatching Roland from his horse, and held him high in the air.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Frightened, his warhorse ran off into the distance, never to be seen again.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Just as the battle looked to be lost, Lady Oder furrowed her brow, drew her long sword, and charged.

items.speaker: "Oder"
items.text: "Ah—"

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: She leaped from her horse high into the air, and drew a long slash across Felgert's bulbous belly.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Accompanying her strike came the self-same shower of yellow sparks.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: But this time the giant let out a gurgling hiss of pain.

items.speaker: "Roland"
items.text: "The navel, the navel—"

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Sir Roland shouted breathlessly.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Oder heard him and turned to look at Felgert.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: There had been no trace of damage in her slash across Felgert's belly, save for a hint of blood around his putrid belly button.

items.speaker: "Oder"
items.text: "Aha, I've found the heel of Achilles!"

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Lady Oder's heart filled with hope at the thought. And she raised her sword again—

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: But the giant's rage was directed elsewhere. His grip on Roland began to tighten.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Sir Roland gave out an agonized scream!

items.speaker: "Roland"
items.text: "Arghh—"

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: But Oder's sword proved the swifter tool, as she pierced the giant's navel in the nick of time!

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: The goliath shuddered and collapsed.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: But in death, the giant's fingers remained tightly wrapped around the knight. And blood ran down his knuckles.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Oder withdrew her sword from the belly of the giant.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: They had won the duel.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Mr. APPLe, the story is finished. You may lower the lights.
The lights fade.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: What do you think of the story?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: It ended too soon. Your Lady Oder defeated the giant. She should go back to be honored for her accomplishment and become a true knight.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Really, you've omitted the most crucial part. Perhaps some ivory tower snobs might appreciate your ambiguity, but the masses will demand a satisfactory end for your heroine.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: I agree! The story ends too soon! Lady Oder deserves more to her tale!

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: She should return to the castle and be generously rewarded with land and riches!

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: With enough wealth of her own, she might go back and build her own house—so that she could have a new future away from her father.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: I confess, sadly, that Lady Oder never was to be knighted. For even after besting the giant, she chose to leave Brittany. She carried on, ever dedicated to the life of freedom she had long sought.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: She traveled far and wide across the land in those days, and when she could, she would write to Sir Roland and Oliver recounting her adventures.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: She won a castle in a duel, and ever unwilling to be tied to the land, she chose to distribute its treasure among the local peasants. A story of that persists in legend.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Later still, she met Lady Berguin, with whom she shared many interests. They became lifelong friends and the closest of confidantes.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Of course, her letters were the source of much inspiration, and many of Someone's greatest jokes.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Someone cannot truly know if Lady Oder was satisfied with this ending.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Yet it is enough to say the story is true.

items.speaker: A Knight
items.text: Although, it must be confessed, for ease of narration, some slight adjustments were made.

items.speaker: All
items.text: Boo—
A Knight's little audience are clearly unhappy with this ending. A Knight seems to pause, as if taken at a loss for words.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Even if I disagree with the institution of landed nobility on principle, I see no reason why she couldn't be knighted before she goes off on her travels.

items.speaker: An-an Lee
items.text: And if nothing else, why was she never given a reward for killing that giant?! That's not fair!
TO BE CONTINUED…
